description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2023: Influence of Different Building Damage Prediction Models on Regional-scale Seismic Risk Estimates is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Matthew DeJong, University of California Berkeley (berkeley.edu). The goal of this study is to evaluate two building damage prediction models, namely, the HAZUS and MDOF-Lu models, that have not been previously compared, to understand and inform users how they differ and may influence civil infrastructure seismic risk assessments. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-8r3q-zx71. Keywords: NHERI SimCenter, Regional Resilience Determination Tool, building damage prediction models, seismic risk estimates, engineering demand parameters, damage measures. Published 2023-08-17. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
